overall_assessment: All 28 packet entries were reviewed in full, including their displayed removed spans; no confirmed personal-data leaks or residual administrative date stamps were found. The suspect flags are false alarms in the displayed material: phone/name_like matches are bibliographic numbers, links, authors, titles or organisations; admin_date matches are publication or regulation dates; and large removed shares mainly reflect staff blocks, library resolver URLs and literal markup. One unflagged random control reveals over-removal of a survey-period year range in a reading-list reference; the other seven controls show no confirmed defect, and packet truncation limits conclusions about omitted text.

findings.evidence: … i Norge i alderen 18-70 år, [−2010-11−] Helsedirektoratet (2014). Rapport: Anbefalinger om kosthold, …
findings.description: The removed range 2010-11 describes the survey period in a literature reference about adults aged 18–70 in Norway. This is content dating within a reference, which the rubric requires preserving, rather than an administrative academic-year stamp. It occurs in a random control without pre-pass flags.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In R/anonymize.R, .anon_generic() applies .drop_academic_year() to consecutive year ranges from 1990 onward. The .running_text_year guard does not protect a range at the end of a reference line, and the government-document guard only recognises cues within 80 characters on the same line.
findings.suggested_fix: Protect reference entries and survey-period ranges before the generic academic-year substitutions. For an otherwise ambiguous consecutive-year range in literature text, require an explicit administrative cue such as studieår, skoleår or academic year before removal; preserve a range following a survey description such as i Norge i alderen 18-70 år. Add a regression case preserving 2010-11 in this reference while still removing labelled academic-year stamps.
